pc.hero_title: Choose how much Wabi remembers — and how much it watches.
pc.hero_1: Retention, confidentiality and moderation are separate choices. Making chat ephemeral does not pretend the server could not see it while it was live.
pc.hero_2: New DMs and groups start encryption-pending and use experimental encryption once everyone's devices are ready. Sending server-readable instead needs each sender's choice. The encryption has not been independently verified, and it does not hide everything from the server operator.
pc.truth_line: Encryption pending, then experimental encryption · not independently verified
pc.step1_text: This changes what newly created community channels inherit. Existing channels keep their current retention until someone deliberately changes them.
pc.retention_strong: Each channel keeps its own policy.
pc.retention_rest: Timed deletion removes messages from normal history; it does not securely erase event records, backups, or recipients’ copies.
pc.step2_text: Older private rooms, and messages a sender chose to send server-readable, can be read by the server. That does not mean Wabi should inspect them automatically.
pc.reports_only_text: Default. Safety rules do not inspect DM/group message text. Participants can still deliberately report a message.
pc.automation_text: Literal server safety rules may inspect server-readable DM/group text before delivery. It never reaches messages sent with experimental encryption.
pc.spaces_text: Server-side content rules apply to community spaces, not private conversations.
pc.step3_text: Ephemeral does not become secretly permanent “just in case.” Evidence is preserved when a participant explicitly submits a report.
pc.report_note: The report dialog tells the reporter that the selected message is preserved for this server’s staff. Safety-rule flags create a case reference without another message snapshot. This expiry applies to new reports only; the owner can remove any active snapshot sooner. Backups and text copied into staff comments have separate lifecycles. Wabi does not send reports to a central moderation service.
pc.step4_text: No central Wabi advertising or behavioral profile is created by either choice.
pc.off_text: Prefer the minimum operational counters necessary to run the server.
pc.local_aggregate_text: Permit aggregate Server Center statistics on this instance only.
pc.analytics_caveat: Policy boundary today: Wabi does not have a central analytics upload here. This setting governs the direction of future Server Center analytics; it is not a claim that every existing operational counter disappears when Off.
pc.step5_text: Keep external services visible instead of silently treating them as part of Wabi.
pc.none_policy_text: Wabi core should not send message content to outside processors.
pc.declared_text: Allow explicitly installed integrations to disclose their own data access.
pc.external_caveat: This is a server policy marker today, not a proven sandbox for arbitrary backend plugins. Add-on capability enforcement remains a separate security boundary.
pc.never_means_text: Live/ephemeral = “not retained,” not “invisible to the running server.”
pc.encrypted_text: Server-side rules can't read messages sent with experimental encryption. Reporting can still disclose selected evidence from the participant’s client.
pc.no_downgrade_text: An encrypted conversation must never become server-readable because an admin changed a moderation option.

privacy_page.meta_description: Privacy information for the Wabi open-source communication project and the default Wabi distribution.
privacy_page.lede: Wabi is built to be self-hostable. That means the operator of the server you use can matter as much as the Wabi software itself.
privacy_page.p_scope: This page describes the Wabi project and the default Wabi distribution. A third-party or self-hosted Wabi instance may be configured differently and may publish its own privacy terms. When an instance-specific policy conflicts with this page, ask that instance operator how it handles data.
privacy_page.p_info: Depending on how an instance is configured and which features you use, Wabi may process account information, profile information, messages and attachments, workspace content, call or connection metadata, device and session information, settings, and security-related logs needed to operate the service.
privacy_page.p_storage: Wabi is designed for independent hosting. Content and account data are generally handled by the Wabi instance you connect to, while some preferences and offline data may also be stored on your device. Instance operators are responsible for their own hosting, backups, retention, access controls, and infrastructure providers.
privacy_page.p_messages_1: New DMs and groups start encryption-pending and use experimental encryption once everyone's devices are ready. Sending server-readable instead needs each sender's choice. The encryption has not been independently verified, and it does not hide everything from the server operator. Older private rooms keep the policy they started with, and community channels are server-readable. A private conversation limits which community members can access it; that is separate from encryption.
privacy_page.p_messages_2: Deleting a message or choosing timed retention does not guarantee secure erasure from event records, backups, logs, or recipients' devices. Device-local Notes and Planner data also have their own browser storage and backup lifecycle. Ask your instance operator about the retention and recovery policy for that server.
privacy_page.p_analytics: The default Wabi project does not require advertising trackers or behavioral advertising. If privacy-respecting aggregate telemetry is introduced in a hosted Wabi service, this policy should be updated before that data collection is relied upon. Independent instance operators may make different choices and should disclose them.
privacy_page.p_cookies: Wabi may use browser storage, local databases, caches, or technically necessary session mechanisms to keep you signed in, remember settings, support offline behavior, and keep the application working. The project does not add a consent banner merely for technically necessary storage.
privacy_page.p_sharing: Wabi does not need to sell personal information to operate the project. Data may nevertheless pass through infrastructure selected by an instance operator, such as hosting, relay, storage, authentication, or networking providers. Features or add-ons that connect to outside services may also send information to those services when you choose to use them.
privacy_page.p_security: Wabi aims to use reasonable technical safeguards, but no software or network service can guarantee absolute security. Server operators should keep their Wabi deployment and dependencies current, restrict administrative access, and use appropriate backups and transport security.
privacy_page.p_choices: Your available account, deletion, export, or retention controls can depend on the instance you use and its operator. For instance-specific requests, contact that server operator. For issues with the Wabi project itself, use the project contact channels linked from the Wabi repository or website.
privacy_page.p_changes: This policy may change as Wabi adds features or hosted services. Material changes should be reflected on this page with the effective date shown on this page.
